mustKnow.item: Thesis: cash-secured put selling framed as selling insurance; only on stocks you want to own ('get paid to name your price'); not guaranteed, most options traders lose
30-delta sweet spot (Goldman 10-yr put-selling study, Sharpe), ~7/10 expire OTM; 30-45 DTE theta window; early-assignment risk concentrated in final week at high delta
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge has 30 delta and 30-45 DTE but not the early-assignment / last-week risk or the study basis.

mustKnow.item: Checklist: own it anyway, real company, enough IV; tight bid-ask spread
Risks: assignment (need the cash), capped upside vs rally (covered-call student anecdote, 200k->215k)
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge garbles the upside cap (see fidelity).

mustKnow.item: Evidence of results: student Denny ~$72k/yr (~$6k/mo) on ~$250k; title claim $3k/month student; creator scaled $100k->$700k
mustKnow.note: Ours has Denny numbers; neither mentions the $3k/month student or the $700k account.

ours.text: Omission: 'the speaker stated a $153 breakeven on a $165 strike put with $1.85 premium; mathematical breakeven is $163.15, indicating an uncorrected source discrepancy.'
ours.problem: False accusation of the creator. The premium is ~$11.85 ('you get 12 bucks', 'gain of $1,185'), so 165-11.85 = ~153 is right. '$1.85' is an ASR garble. The system flagged a correct number as an error.

ours.text: Call: PLTR 'long', conviction high, 'Continuously sell put options on Palantir as long as the creator favors the stock'
ours.problem: Overstates direction. The creator says PLTR is 'tapped out for gains' and he doesn't see it going up much short term. The stance is neutral-to-mildly-bullish income, not a high-conviction long. It also duplicates the Nov-20 call.

ours.text: Three separate Google calls ('conditional', 'medium') describing the same assignment
ours.problem: Duplicate calls. Commentary on managing an already-assigned position, not a new recommendation, is presented as three calls.

ours.text: tickerSentiment Google: mixed bullish/neutral across 7 entries
ours.problem: Inconsistent stance for one name. The creator is explicit: 'I'm a firm believer in Google.'
False call. The creator only notes an ITM put he will have to manage; there is no thesis.

leapedge.text: 'Selling puts limits upside potential, as you do not benefit from stock price appreciation beyond the strike price plus the collected premium.'
leapedge.problem: Mechanically wrong. A short put's gain is capped at the premium, independent of the strike. 'Beyond strike plus premium' describes a covered call.

leapedge.text: PLTR trade idea stance 'long', conviction 'high', verdict '1 LONG'
leapedge.problem: A short put on a stock the creator calls 'tapped out' is labeled a high-conviction LONG. This overstates directional conviction and hides the instrument; the 'instrument' field is null.

leapedge.text: Quote '...number one strategy that I would be using on Palantir right now'
leapedge.problem: Minor. The quote is cleaned up; the transcript reads 'on pound right now'. The meaning is preserved.

sentimentIssues: 15 tickerSentiment rows for 6 names; Google appears 7 times with alternating bullish/neutral and long/conditional.
PLTR is marked 'bullish/long' although the creator says it is 'tapped out' short term. Better: bullish long-term, neutral short-term, expressed via short puts.
NBIS marked 'bullish/long' only because a short put 'did really well'. That is a P&L remark, not a stated view.
QQQ 'long' is acceptable, but the view is really 'good put-selling vehicle for ETF-only investors'.
why: Ours captures the live position book (GOOGL assignment math, MSFT, NBIS, QQQ), the early-assignment risk and the 175/165 alternatives, and LeapEdge reports none of that. Ours is still only narrowly better. It fabricates a numeric 'discrepancy' against the creator, leaves GOOGL/MSFT unresolved, splits one GOOGL situation into three calls, and buries the content under 11 pipeline-housekeeping omissions. LeapEdge is clean but thin: one PLTR idea without premium, breakeven or delta.
recommendations: Add explicit option fields to calls: instrument ('short put'), strike, expiry, premium, breakeven, delta. The PLTR idea should read: 'Sell PLTR Nov-20 165P @ ~$11.85, breakeven ~153, delta 0.35; alt ATM 175P @ ~$16'.

Do not second-guess numbers with an ASR-naive calculator. Before publishing a 'discrepancy', cross-check other mentions ('12 bucks', '$1,185'). The '$1.85 -> 163.15' omission is an error by ours, not by the source.
Separate 'existing position management' (GOOGL assigned, MSFT ITM, NBIS/QQQ expiring) into a 'Disclosed positions' table, not calls. Keep calls for forward-looking ideas.
Deduplicate calls and tickerSentiment per ticker: one row per name with a consolidated stance and the strongest quote.
Resolve common company names deterministically (Google->GOOGL, Microsoft->MSFT, Palanteer/Palunteer->PLTR) before emitting; never emit ticker null for mega-caps.
Stance for short puts should be 'bullish-income / neutral', not 'long high conviction', when the creator says upside is 'tapped out'.
Remove pipeline-internal text from brief.omissions ('source-0: Full-source recall is a bounded model review...', 'Optional calculation for s13 withheld'). A PM sees noise, not omissions.
